name: Wutong Dawn Breath (Ngô Đồng Triêu Tức Quyết)
concept: The outer gate's method, breathed at dawn facing east the way the wutong grows toward the morning sun. Wood qi is drawn up like sap and burned slowly at the top of the breath, so a Wood root learns to be kindling and a Fire root learns to rise without flaring.
lore: Ngô Thê Đồng wrote it on the ridge in 486, the year after he opened Thiều Âm Thị (A238), for children of the bamboo villages who had more Wood in them than Fire.

name: Five-Virtue Phoenix Canon (Ngũ Đức Phượng Hoàng Kinh)

effects.name: Birds Pay Court to the Phoenix
effects.rule: Each hit your bird companions land lays on you the next Five-Colour Plumage colour you lack, at most once a pulse. Each time you spend a full plumage (five colours), you heal 3 % of your maximum health and your companions' next hits deal 30 % more.

concept: The founder's method. The canon opens five marks in the meridians, each lit by Fire and fed by Wood. In a fight each art lays a plumage stack in one of five colours; at five colours the holder spends them for damage and healing.
lore: Ngô Thê Đồng wrote the first four marks on the ridge between 480 and 590 and could not light the fifth until he sat by Chúc Dung Khẩu in 592.

name: Morning Sun Feather Fan (Triêu Dương Vũ Phiến Quyết)
concept: The palace's fighting art and the reason its disciples carry fans instead of swords. A fan stroke throws burning feathers, each a Fire stack; the closed fan is a guard; the open fan turned edge-on cuts.
lore: Nguyên Chước Ly took it from the founder's dawn breath and made it a war art in the Vermilion Caves (584-590).

name: Shao Remnant Score (Thiều Âm Tàn Phổ)

effects.name: Playing Past the Break
effects.rule: Once a fight, firing Remnant Score's Next Movement right after its seventh attempts the eighth movement via a counted-chance meter.

concept: What the scattered Vân Môn musicians remembered of the Shao after Cửu Thiều fell (A251), written down by Liên Khánh Dao in the founder's time. Seven movements are written; the score breaks off where the eighth should begin.
lore: Taught only in the Hall of Rites at the Wutong Court, on bamboo flutes from Tử Trúc Lâm.

name: Nine Shao Phoenix Advent (Cửu Thành Lai Nghi Kinh)
concept: The head's method, written by the founder from the Tiêu Thiều Quản itself after he found it in 485 (C097). Each movement is an art lifting the player's Fire and laying Shao stacks on every hearer; the ninth at layer 15 is forbidden.
lore: Only two people have read it whole: the founder and Hoa Triêu Dương.

name: Hearth-Ash Breathing (Lô Hôi Thổ Nạp Pháp)
concept: An Earth breathing method passed among the servants tending the palace hearths and lower terrace beds, keeping the body steady beside the Fire halls above without entering the lineage.
lore: Kept by the sweepers and porters below the Fire Court; teaches no Fire and opens no inner gate.
